# SK4010 — A `Where` the next operator could have taken as its predicate

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`xs.Where(p).First()` is `xs.First(p)`: one fewer iterator object and one fewer delegate hop per element.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Performance |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.0 |

## Why

`Enumerable.Where` allocates an iterator that the next operator then wraps and drives, so every element crosses two `MoveNext` frames instead of one. `First`, `FirstOrDefault`, `Last`, `LastOrDefault`, `Single`, `SingleOrDefault`, `Any`, `Count` and `LongCount` each have an overload that takes the predicate directly and does the same work in one loop with no intermediate object. LINQ defines the two forms to select the same elements in the same order for the same predicate, so this is a rewrite with no semantic content — which is why it is worth a rule rather than a review comment: the longer form reads no better and costs an indirection per element.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
var first = items.Where(item => item.IsReady).First();
var ready = items.Where(item => item.IsReady).Count();
```

Write:

```csharp
var first = items.First(item => item.IsReady);
var ready = items.Count(item => item.IsReady);
```

## When it does not fire

Both calls must resolve to `System.Linq.Enumerable`. A `Where` or a `First` on `System.Linq.Queryable` is never reported, because a provider is free to translate the one-argument overload and not the predicate one; nor is a user-defined `Where`, a user-defined operator of the same name, or either call when the symbol did not resolve. The `Where` must be the `Func<T, bool>` overload: the indexed `Func<T, int, bool>` form has no counterpart on any of the consuming operators, so it is left alone. The consuming call must pass no arguments of its own and must be one of the nine operators whose predicate overload is defined to iterate identically — `Where(p).All(q)`, `Where(p).Sum(f)` and `Where(p).Select(f)` are different shapes and are not reported. A conditional access (`xs?.Where(p).First()`) is not reported, because the rewrite has to move the member binding rather than replace a name. ⚠ The one observable difference the rewrite does make is the text of the exception on an empty sequence: `Where(p).First()` throws `InvalidOperationException("Sequence contains no elements")` and `First(p)` throws `InvalidOperationException("Sequence contains no matching element")`. The type is the same and the condition is the same; a test asserting on the message string would see the change.
